title: Dedicated throughput recovery matrix and notification procedures
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description: Goal: Produce a clear, auditable definition and operational flow for measuring and remediating dedicated throughput shortfalls that can be embedded into customer contracts and the Console. Scope includes the SLA metric definition, error-budget computation window, automated detection thresholds, escalation & notification steps, credit calculation examples, dispute/arbitration timeline, and the runbook for product/ops/legal to execute credits and communicate with customers. Excludes billing system implementation (handled by Finance) and detailed on-prem upgrade playbooks.
acceptance_criteria: One-line formal SLA metric and measurement window documented and signed off by Legal and Reliability
Error budget formula and sample computations for three customer tiers (small/medium/enterprise) included
Automated detection thresholds wired to Console alerts with example dashboard tile
Notification templates (email + Console banner + status page incident) for initial notice, remediation progress, and credit issuance
Credit schedule matrix that maps percentage degradation to monetary credit, with examples and rounding rules
Runbook for ops/solutions to follow from detection through customer credit and post-mortem
Contract clause draft suitable for inclusion in Dedicated Capacity MSA and one-page customer FAQ
notes: Measurement window: recommend 30-day rolling window for entitlement measurement + 7-day stabilization after an operator-induced failover

Metric definition: 'Serve Capacity Availability (SCA)' = sum(available_tokens_served) / sum(promised_tokens) aggregated at the customer-az level, computed per-hour and rolled into a 30-day quantile (p95) to reduce noise
Error budget: budget = promised_tokens * 0.99 (for 1% allowed degradation) -> daily burn rate computed from hourly SCA deviations

Credit computation: linear slab bands (e.g., 0-2% no credit, 2-10% 5% credit, 10-30% 20% credit, >30% contact sales/legal) with minimum credit floor of $50; we considered exponential and settled on slabs for predictability
Detection thresholds: automated alert when hourly SCA < 95th percentile of baseline for >3 consecutive hours; preliminary rule triggers investigation pipeline before customer notice
Notification cadence: initial notice within 60 minutes of confirmed degradation; progress updates at 4h, 12h, 24h; final credit notice within 5 business days after incident closure
Dispute timeline: customer disputes must be raised within 30 days of final notice; arbitration window is 45 days; during arbitration, interim credits may be issued at Redwood discretion
Trade-offs: shorter windows (7-14d) quicker feedback but more sensitive to transient load patterns; longer windows (60d) blunt short incidents — chosen 30d as a balance
Out-of-scope: hourly per-model latency guarantees, per-request quality regressions — these live in separate SLOs/PRDs
